messages:
zoe-docs: spotted a small but recurring issue in quickstart: the Node snippet uses top-level await without mentioning Node version or alternative, and the env var name differs from other examples. New users hit SyntaxError or find undefined env var.

ash-support: confirmed, a customer pasted the snippet into an older Node container and got a crash. Also saw confusion over REDWOOD_KEY vs REDWOOD_API_KEY.

felix-sdk: proposed minimal edits: show both an async wrapper and top-level await variant, and standardize env var to REDWOOD_API_KEY. Example:
```js
// top-level await (Node >=16.8)
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1', prompt: 'Hey' })
console.log(res.output)
// or, for older Node versions:
;(async () => { const res = await client.generate(...); console.log(res.output) })()
```

anya-devex: will open a tiny PR to patch quickstart, include a one-liner about Node versions, and add a CI smoke test that runs the snippet with a mock server. Keeping examples terse but explicit avoids this class of onboarding friction.

deploy-bot: docs preview queued by anya-devex: https://deploy-preview.redwood.ai/quickstart/1123 (expires in 24h) :white_check_mark:

zoe-docs: preview looks good, thanks. Filing a follow-up to scan other language snippets for env var parity. Closing after merge. :thumbsup:
